idiom_name: enum type (full class, one instance per constant)
implementation_notes: Since Java 5 the language feature absorbs the classic Typesafe Enum pattern: an enum declaration defines a full-fledged class whose constants are public static final instances, effectively final because no accessible constructor exists, with their own namespace and compile-time type safety - an int or a String is never assignable to it. Members take constructor data and methods (constant-specific bodies or a strategy enum), and EnumSet/EnumMap replace bit fields and ordinal-indexed arrays. The hand-written class of the pre-5 pattern is needed only when targeting Java 1.4 or older.
pitfalls: ordinal() is declaration order: persisting it makes every insert or reorder a data migration; use name() or an explicit key.
A classic switch statement over an enum is not required to be exhaustive - adding a constant compiles silently; switch expressions (Java 14+) and constant-specific bodies do get compiler checking.
Enum constants are singletons: they are serialized by name (renaming breaks persisted data) and any mutable state on them is global.
